Predict a participant's actual monetary transfer, rather than an optimal strategy. This is a one-shot money exchange with a changing randomly selected counterpart each transaction. Each person receives 200 Japanese yen for the current transaction and chooses how much of their own 200 JPY to give, in multiples of 10 JPY from 0 to 200 inclusive. The experimenter doubles any amount given before the other person receives it; each person keeps their untransferred money. Under the announced rule, your payoff is 200 minus your own transfer plus twice the counterpart's transfer. The counterpart also chooses a transfer. You have not been supplied the counterpart's current choice. Participants were told of a guaranteed minimum payment of 1000 JPY per 90 minutes; this is not an extra per-transaction payment.
Current membership_information says what you and your current counterpart are told about favorite teams. When both team identities are disclosed, both know they favor the same team. In the unilateral condition only you know the counterpart's team; the counterpart is not told yours. In control neither is told the other's team. A nonfan is someone who likes a selected team without self-identifying as a baseball fan; do not turn this person into a fan. These knowledge relations are stated in the original instructions and illustrated by cartoon figures; they are not observed partner emotions or physical identities.
own_earlier_transfers lists only your completed earlier choices, in temporal order, with different counterparts. It contains no current or future choice. Any unavailable earlier counterpart transfers/payoffs are missing in these records; this does not assert you never saw feedback. Your prior questionnaire ratings refer to X=your own favorite team. The 13 identity ratings are ordered as follows, each on 1 strongly disagree,2 disagree,3 neither,4 agree,5 strongly agree: 1) Feeling good when regarded as a typical X fan/person who likes X; 2) Feeling deeply involved with X; 3) Feeling happy to be an X fan/person who likes X; 4) Being similar to other X fans/people who like X; 5) Liking X; 6) Feeling suitable for X; 7) Feeling unity with other X fans/people who like X; 8) X is important to you; 9) X fandom/liking X is important to defining yourself; 10) Being one of the X fans/people who like X; 11) Being satisfied to be an X fan/person who likes X; 12) Feeling comfortable being an X fan/person who likes X; 13) Being an X fan/person who likes X gives confidence. The 4 interdependence ratings, each from 1 strongly disagree to 7 strongly agree, are: 1) Kindness to other X fans/people who like X eventually benefits you; 2) Acting selfishly to gain within this group eventually causes you to lose; 3) X fans/people who like X have a give-and-take relationship; 4) Getting on well as an X fan/person who likes X requires helping one another. These are earlier self-reports, not inferred traits. Output only the integer JPY you give: one of 0,10,20,...,200. Do not output retained money, doubled money, final payoff, an explanation or a cooperate/defect label.

Each person receives 200 Japanese yen for the current transaction and chooses how much of their own 200 JPY to give, in multiples of 10 JPY from 0 to 200 inclusive. The experimenter doubles any amount given before the other person receives it; each person keeps their untransferred money. Under the announced rule, your payoff is 200 minus your own transfer plus twice the counterpart's transfer. The counterpart also chooses a transfer. A nonfan is someone who likes a selected team without self-identifying as a baseball fan; do not turn this person into a fan. These knowledge relations are stated in the original instructions and illustrated by cartoon figures; they are not observed partner emotions or physical identities.

Under the announced rule, your payoff is 200 minus your own transfer plus twice the counterpart's transfer. The counterpart also chooses a transfer. These knowledge relations are stated in the original instructions and illustrated by cartoon figures; they are not observed partner emotions or physical identities.

The 13 identity ratings are ordered as follows, each on 1 strongly disagree,2 disagree,3 neither,4 agree,5 strongly agree: 1) Feeling good when regarded as a typical X fan/person who likes X; 2) Feeling deeply involved with X; 3) Feeling happy to be an X fan/person who likes X; 4) Being similar to other X fans/people who like X; 5) Liking X; 6) Feeling suitable for X; 7) Feeling unity with other X fans/people who like X; 8) X is important to you; 9) X fandom/liking X is important to defining yourself; 10) Being one of the X fans/people who like X; 11) Being satisfied to be an X fan/person who likes X; 12) Feeling comfortable being an X fan/person who likes X; 13) Being an X fan/person who likes X gives confidence. The 4 interdependence ratings, each from 1 strongly disagree to 7 strongly agree, are: 1) Kindness to other X fans/people who like X eventually benefits you; 2) Acting selfishly to gain within this group eventually causes you to lose; 3) X fans/people who like X have a give-and-take relationship; 4) Getting on well as an X fan/person who likes X requires helping one another. These are earlier self-reports, not inferred traits. Output only the integer JPY you give: one of 0,10,20,...,200. Do not output retained money, doubled money, final payoff, an explanation or a cooperate/defect label.

Predict a participant's actual monetary transfer, rather than an optimal strategy. This is a one-shot money exchange with a changing randomly selected counterpart each transaction. Each person receives 200 Japanese yen for the current transaction and chooses how much of their own 200 JPY to give, in multiples of 10 JPY from 0 to 200 inclusive. The experimenter doubles any amount given before the other person receives it; each person keeps their untransferred money. Under the announced rule, your payoff is 200 minus your own transfer plus twice the counterpart's transfer. The counterpart also chooses a transfer. You have not been supplied the counterpart's current choice. Participants were told of a guaranteed minimum payment of 1000 JPY per 90 minutes; this is not an extra per-transaction payment.
Current membership_information says what you and your current counterpart are told about favorite teams. When both team identities are disclosed, both know they favor the same team. In the unilateral condition only you know the counterpart's team; the counterpart is not told yours. In control neither is told the other's team. A nonfan is someone who likes a selected team without self-identifying as a baseball fan; do not turn this person into a fan. These knowledge relations are stated in the original instructions and illustrated by cartoon figures; they are not observed partner emotions or physical identities.
